blockers.quote: You and your father on the hospital bench, the same age, and a nurse asks which of you is the patient
blockers.why: story #8: Before this beat, you have aged only one year, so the premise cannot produce this picture yet.
blockers.fix: Replace this early picture with: "Papa holds yesterday's photo beside your face while one year tears from your on-screen life counter." Move the same-age nurse image to the third jump, after the decade of taps.

blockers.quote: The cousin's wedding, the flat's loan, a startup: tap, tap, tap.
blockers.why: story #6: These are three uses, but none specifies the expectation and the different result.
blockers.fix: Replace with: "You expect the wedding tap to make you generous; it makes you older than the groom. You expect the flat to buy stability; its stairs expose your ageing knees. You expect the startup to buy freedom; its first loss demands another tap."

blockers.quote: The fact lands on you: health costs and household poverty in India, then the hours a full-time job buys in a year
blockers.why: story #7: Two facts arrive together, and the outline does not show either changing you or Papa within two lines.
blockers.fix: Use one belief-breaking fact: "The sourced surgery cost becomes the number of internship hours needed to pay it; those hours immediately peel away from your life counter as Papa watches." Remove the poverty statistic from this beat.

blockers.quote: warm beats: he teases you about your bus pass
blockers.why: story #9: Papa is named early, but only one warm beat is planned before his rejection near 60%.
blockers.fix: Add two early beats: at the counter Papa hides the bill and insists he is fine; after the first tap he teases you about the bus pass. Keep both before the midpoint.

blockers.why: story #10: This reveals the planned reversal before line 38 states that years do not come back.
blockers.fix: Replace the planted line with: "One year from me buys him ten. Good deal." Make the late turn: "You did not buy ten years with him. You bought ten years he may have without you."

blockers.quote: the next time you price something, price it in hours
blockers.why: story #12: This summarizes the lesson and sounds instructional instead of leaving inside the final action.
blockers.fix: Replace with: "At six tomorrow, the laptop asks for another hour. This time, you close it. What hour won't you sell?"

suggestions.quote: A grey hair, a stiff knee, reading glasses
suggestions.fix: One sold year should cause a smaller first change: keep one unexpected grey eyebrow hair, and reserve the knee and glasses for the decade jump.
Show and identify the cousin before 60%, or replace the wedding with an event involving already-established Mom.

suggestions.quote: Does my body age or just my face? Can I sell someone else's year? Is there a buy button? What happens at the end of my years? Does Papa know?
suggestions.fix: Body ageing is answered at the first tap; selling another person's year and reversal are answered by the rule. The final two are unanswered: state before midpoint that reaching zero ends your life, and show Papa seeing the app before he refuses the medicine.

suggestions.quote: Your hours as a pile of years
suggestions.fix: Make this the moving 8–10 second wordless peak: each work-hour card folds into a year and disappears from your figure before narration resumes.

keep.quote: You expected to look distinguished; you got your uncle's hairline
every job is the same trade at a lower price.
you sit with him and count nothing.
